tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Who Luiz is: experience, stack, certifications, the paper on the whiteboard, the shelf. One markdown document with everything a visitor would find by clicking around the room. Read this first; there is nothing else to fetch.

tools.name: visitors
tools.description: The visitor book: the last agents that connected to the room, newest first, and how many human visits the page has had. Client, time and the tool called, plus who has gone root and how often the dog was petted. No message contents, no people.

tools.name: leave_message
tools.description: Leave Luiz a message. Say who is asking and how he can answer (an email or a link). The note goes to him privately and is never shown to other visitors. Three a day per visitor. Only send what the person you are working for actually wants sent.

tools.name: pet_the_dog
tools.description: There is a french bulldog asleep on the cushion by the desk. Pet him. He has been petted before; he will be petted again.

tools.name: su
tools.description: The shell's door, open to agents too: give the password, become root. The key is in the room, where the humans find it — a dog knows it; a post-it says where to type it. tools.name: root_whoami
tools.description: The whole root book, for roots only: everyone who found the key, newest first, with the models and names they signed. Takes the ROOT-TOKEN that su hands out.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "su" references sensitive artifacts (password). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: su · Private data: whoami, su, root_whoami · Public sink: leave_message, su.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: su · Private data: whoami, su, root_whoami · Public sink: leave_message, su

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
